titulo: Fingertip study reveals pain threshold during millimeter-wave exposure
resumo: Wireless technologies using millimeter waves are becoming increasingly important for high-speed communication, but their effects on human health need to be better understood. Heating of the skin is a well-established effect of exposure at these frequencies, yet the temperature at which people begin to experience pain remains uncertain. Previous studies using different heat sources have reported varying pain thresholds, while evidence from direct millimeter-wave exposure in highly sensitive areas, such as the fingertip, has been limited. Understanding when sensations progress from warmth to pain could help inform safer exposure guidelines.

titulo: Redict deprecated in favor of Valkey
resumo: Drew DeVault has announced that Redict , a fork of Redis that was created in response to Redis's 2024 license change , has been deprecated. He recommends switching to Valkey , the permissively licensed Redis fork supported by the Linux Foundation. The two projects are mutually compatible, so switching should be as simple as changing which package is installed and renaming the configuration file. I had hoped to rally the Redis diaspora around a copyleft initiative, to protect ourselves from future rug-pulls, and made Redict to serve this purpose. However, with the valkey project's success, and Redis's return to a copyleft license, Redict was not able to build a sustainable community. We recommend that Redict users switch to valkey, which uses a permissive license but has better long-term prospects. We advise against switching back to Redis; though it is once again open source, and copyleft, it uses a contributor license agreement which will facilitate another rug-pull when Redis has a bad financial quarter.

titulo: Measurements reveal link between quantum spin and sound-carrying vibrations in an ultrathin semiconductor
resumo: Researchers at the UCLA Samueli School of Engineering and Auburn University have achieved a scientific first: They measured atomic vibrations that carry heat and sound waves, and connected them to a quantum property called spin, which is a way of characterizing a subatomic particle's built-in magnetism.

titulo: These Engineers Are Cleaning Up Connected Cars’ Security Flaws
resumo: Today’s connected vehicles collect and transmit far more personal data from drivers and passengers than their predecessors, with costly consequences. The Center for Automotive Management in Germany estimates that cyberattacks have caused more than $20 billion in damage to the auto industry as of 2025, twenty times higher than in 2022. This week, engineers and cybersecurity researchers are gathering in Bonn, Germany, for the Embedded Security in Cars (escar) conference to discuss using AI for defense, hardening chips, and otherwise securing the auto industry’s data handling. Frank Kargl , an escar Europe co-organizer and director of the Institute of Distributed Systems at Ulm University in Germany, says that recent cyberattacks on infrastructure like supermarket refrigerators all over Europe have highlighted the risk of a broad hack of automobiles that aims to cause arbitrary damage . titulo: Euclid's H-alpha observations map where stars form in distant galaxies
resumo: Euclid was launched into space in July 2023 to explore two of astronomy's biggest mysteries: dark matter and dark energy. The space telescope's first major data release covers some 1,900 square degrees of the sky, equivalent to around 14% of the area planned for the six-year mission and around 5% of the total sky. It is an unprecedented collection of visible and near-infrared observations.
